predecessors.note: The Lunda core commune is kiLunda-speaking; the page names Luba-speaking peoples as neighbours and the origin of Nawej's father. No dossier is implied for the Luba as a predecessor state beyond the royal marriage.

successors.note: Lunda page: 'At the start of the colonial era (1884), the heartland was divided among Portuguese Angola, the Congo Free State, and British North-Western Rhodesia.'

the part in British North-Western Rhodesia

capitals.name: Musumba
capitals.note: Coordinates 8°21′41″S 22°38′32″E from the Musumba page (a geohack link on the same page gives 8°33′S 22°41′E). The Lunda page says only 'The royal centre of the empire was called musumba'; neither page dates the capital or any move.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1709, but the page dates the title Mwane-a-Yamvu to c. 1665 and the kingdom's 150,000 km2 to 'by 1680'. Drawn as a disc of that area around Musumba (confidence 1 for the shape; the page names no boundary).

correction.text: about 150,000 km2 around Musumba: 'The Lunda Kingdom controlled some 150,000 km2 by 1680'

keyframe_review.note: Wrong place: the shape (112,401 km2; bbox 12.2-16.2 E, 8.3-4.6 S) lies in Kongo country (Bas-Congo and Zaire province), a copy of the Kongo footprint, not in Lunda country (Kasai, Lunda Norte/Sul and Katanga, 18-26 E). Its area is 0.75 of the infobox 150,000 km2 (1680) so the size is plausible. Corrected to a 150,000 km2 disc around Musumba; the 18th-century expansions (past the Kasai River in the 1720s, 'the 1730s and 1740s and into the 1750s') are ledger gains.

correction.text: about 300,000 km2 around Musumba: 'doubled in size to around 300,000 km2 at its height in the 19th century'

keyframe_review.note: Wrong place and too small: 109,111 km2 against the page's 'around 300,000 km2 at its height in the 19th century' (ratio 0.36, beyond a factor of two), and located on the Kongo footprint. Corrected to a 300,000 km2 disc around Musumba (the page does not date the height; the ledger's 1856 gain is a bridge at confidence 1).

correction.text: the 19th-century extent, held until the Chokwe overthrow; Cliopatria's years 1888-1889 should be dropped

keyframe_review.note: Wrong place, and the row runs two years past the page's end: the infobox gives '17th century-1887'. Corrected to the 300,000 km2 disc, valid to 1887; the page says the heartland was already divided on paper among Portuguese Angola, the Congo Free State and British North-Western Rhodesia in 1884.

region.text: about 150,000 km2 around Musumba: 'The Lunda Kingdom controlled some 150,000 km2 by 1680'

ledger.note: c. 1665: the Mwane-a-Yamvu title is created and the Lunda kingdom begins. 'Their son became the first paramount ruler and created the title Mwane-a-Yamvu (c. 1665).' Other sources make Nawej, ruling 'about 1695', the first well-attested ruler; the Early Congolese history page has Mwata Yamvo 'ruler from 1660 to 1665'. Infobox start '17th century'.

region.text: 'expansion pushed past the Kasai River to the west'

ledger.note: 1720s: under Yava a Nawej the Lunda expand west across the Kasai River; the Lulua resisted. 'In the 1720s or so, under Yava, expansion pushed past the Kasai River to the west.' The Musumba page adds 'As the Lunda Empire expanded in the 1730s and 1740s and into the 1750s'; neither page names the land of those later steps.

region.text: the ring between the 150,000 km2 core and the 300,000 km2 extent

ledger.note: The kingdom doubles in size. 'It doubled in size to around 300,000 km2 at its height in the 19th century.' The page gives no year; 1856 is where Cliopatria's second shape begins (confidence 1, a bridge).

region.text: about 300,000 km2 around Musumba: 'doubled in size to around 300,000 km2 at its height in the 19th century'

ledger.note: 1887: the Lunda kingdom ends. Infobox '17th century-1887'; 'The kingdom of Lunda came to an end in the 19th century, when it was invaded by the Chokwe, who were armed with guns.' The Chokwe page: 'By 1900, the Chokwe had overthrown the Lunda kingdom (also called the Mwata Yanvo) altogether.' At the start of the colonial era (1884) the heartland was already divided on paper among Portuguese Angola, the Congo Free State and British North-Western Rhodesia.

wars.name: Chokwe invasion of the Lunda kingdom

zones.text: about 300,000 km2 around Musumba: 'doubled in size to around 300,000 km2 at its height in the 19th century'

wars.outcome: The Chokwe, armed with guns, invaded and overthrew the Lunda kingdom; the infobox ends the kingdom in 1887.
wars.note: The page dates the invasion only to 'the 19th century', so the 'from' year 1801 is a placeholder; the end is the infobox's 1887. The Chokwe page says 'By 1900'. Neither page gives the sack of Musumba as a dated event.

wars.name: Lunda-Kanyok war (Nawej and Muland)
wars.outcome: Nawej was killed by Kanyok forces, who built a fortress in Lunda territory; Muland drove them out.
wars.note: Undated on the page ('about 1695' is only Nawej's accession); years here are approximate and the page gives no border result.

certainty.note: A confederation of chieftainships paying tribute, with no surveyed frontier; the pages give areas, not boundaries.

notes: Cliopatria's three Lunda shapes are on the Kongo footprint (12.2-16.2 E) and are marked wrong; the corrections are discs sized to the page's areas around Musumba because the pages name no boundary (the gazetteer's 'Lunda (region)' is 412,733 km2, bbox 18-26 E, and is used only for the successors' land). Page budget (1-2 pages) was exceeded by one: the Musumba page was opened only for the capital's coordinates. Not settled: the date of the Chokwe sack of Musumba (neither page gives one; 1887 is the infobox's end), the dates of the Kazembe split and of the Kasai expansion beyond '1720s or so', the Mwata Yamvo succession list (none on the page, so no rulers strip), Kasanje and the Imbangala (not on the page). The Chokwe who overthrew the kingdom have no dossier: the Chokwe people page gives no dated polity, boundary or territorial event, so they appear only as the dissolve counterpart and in the Chokwe war entry (see the group report, gaps). Gazetteer: 'Musumba' is not a place (22.64 E, 8.36 S); 'Lunda (region)' has confidence 1.
